title: The deadliest earthquake ever hit homes in cliffs 🏔️
subject: earthquake
description:
Would you run outside or crouch and wait? 👇

On January 23, 1556, an earthquake centered near Huaxian in China's Shaanxi province killed an estimated 830,000 people, the highest death toll of any earthquake on record. Many lived in yaodong, cave homes dug into cliffs of loess, a soft wind-blown silt that collapsed and slid in the shaking. A survivor, the scholar Qin Keda, wrote that people indoors should not rush out but crouch and wait: "Even if the nest has been ruined, the eggs in it may still remain intact."

Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Shaanxi province earthquake of 1556"; History.com, "The Deadliest Earthquake Ever Recorded" (Becky Little); Wikipedia, "1556 Shaanxi earthquake" and "Yaodong".

scenes.text: Whole villages lived inside cliffs of soft yellow dirt.
On January 23, 1556, an earthquake in China's Shaanxi province brought those cliffs down.
The cave homes, called yaodong, were dug into loess, silt that crumbles when it shakes.
Ming dynasty records counted about 830,000 dead, more than any earthquake in history.
A survivor, the scholar Qin Keda, warned against running outside at the first jolt. Crouch and wait.
Even if the nest is ruined, he wrote, the eggs inside may still be intact.
